title: Add --cache flag to reuse parsed results
body:
## Summary

Parsing is the slow part of `logslice` on big files (the 1.2 GB ingest log from the nightly job takes ~40 s just to parse). This PR adds an opt-in on-disk cache of parsed records, so repeated queries against the same file skip parsing entirely.

## Changes

- New `--cache` flag. When set, parsed records are loaded from the cache if present; otherwise the file is parsed and the result is saved for next time.
- New module `logslice/cache.py` with `load()` / `store()`.
- Cache entries are stored as JSON, one file per log file, in the cache directory: `$LOGSLICE_CACHE_DIR` if set, otherwise `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/logslice`, otherwise `~/.cache/logslice`. The directory is resolved when it's needed, not at import time.
- The cache key is computed by `cache_key()` from the file's resolved path, size and mtime, so editing or appending to a log automatically invalidates its entry.
- Entries expire after a configurable TTL: `--cache-ttl SECONDS` (integer, default 3600). `load()` takes a `ttl` keyword argument (default 3600) and treats an entry whose `created_at` is older than that as a miss; the CLI then re-parses and overwrites the entry. Delete the cache directory to clear the cache.
- `--cache` is ignored (with a warning) when reading from stdin.
- README: new "Caching" section.

## Testing

- `pytest`: new `tests/test_cache.py` covers the store/load round trip, key changes on modification, corrupt entries, TTL expiry, and cache-directory resolution (`LOGSLICE_CACHE_DIR`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, default, explicit `directory=`); `tests/test_cli.py` covers the `--cache` hit path, `--cache-ttl` expiry/re-parse, and that nothing is written without the flag.
- Manually: `logslice --cache --count-by level ingest.log` twice; the second run went from 41 s to 0.4 s.

reviews.body:
Thanks Marta, this will help a lot with the big ingest logs. Requesting changes for three things (details in the inline comments):

1. Make the cache directory configurable instead of hard-coding `~/.cache/logslice`.
2. Cache entries need to expire.
3. Small naming nit on `_key`.

comments.body: Nice, I've been wanting this for the ingest logs. No strong opinions on the details, I'll leave the review to Priya.

review_comments.body: nit: `_key` is a bit cryptic, and I'd like to reuse it for a `logslice cache` subcommand later. Please rename it to `cache_key` (public, no underscore) and give it a docstring saying what goes into the key (resolved path, size and mtime).

Done — the directory is now resolved at call time by `cache_dir()`: `$LOGSLICE_CACHE_DIR` (as-is, no subdirectory) → `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/logslice` → `~/.cache/logslice`. An explicit `directory=` argument still wins, and the `--cache` help text no longer hard-codes the path. Added tests for the resolution order and for empty env vars falling through.

review_comments.body: Done — `load()` now takes a `ttl` keyword (default 3600) and treats an entry whose `created_at` is older than that as a miss; the CLI gained `--cache-ttl SECONDS` (integer, default 3600) and re-parses/overwrites on a miss as before. Added tests for expiry (module level and via the CLI).
Renamed to `cache_key` (public) with a docstring noting it hashes the resolved path, size and mtime.
